title: Short Stuff: The Sandman
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Sandman, the folkloric figure who brings sleep and dreams. The hosts open with the 1955 Cordettes hit "Mr. Sandman" and its use in films, then discuss the Sandman's European roots, the crusty eye-sleep explanation for why he sprinkles sand in children's eyes, and the 1816 German E.T.A. Hoffmann tale "Der Sandmann," in which the Sandman steals children's eyes to feed his children on the moon. They then cover Hans Christian Andersen's 1841 fairy tale "Ole Lukøje" (Ole Shut-Eye), which includes his dark brother who brings death, and compare the figure's light and dark duality to Santa Claus and Krampus.

segments.title: Opening banter and Mr. Sandman song
segments.summary: The hosts open with banter about the catchy song 'Mr. Sandman' by the Cordettes, its 1955 hit status, and its use in Halloween and Back to the Future.

segments.title: Sandman folklore and sleep in the eyes
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Sandman as a folkloric figure from Central and Eastern Europe, compare him to Santa Claus, and discuss eye crust (sleep) and why folklore says the Sandman sprinkles sand in children's eyes.

segments.title: Origins of the Sandman in German tradition
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the German origins of the Sandman, the phrase 'der Sandmann kommt' from 18th-century German dictionaries, and how German immigrants may have brought the concept to America.

segments.title: E.T.A. Hoffmann's Der Sandmann
segments.summary: E.T.A. Hoffmann's 1816 story 'Der Sandmann' is described as a horrifying children's tale in which the Sandman throws sand in disobedient children's eyes, collects their eyeballs, and feeds them to his children on the moon. The hosts discuss its function as a bedtime scare tactic.

segments.title: Hans Christian Andersen's Ole Lukøje
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Hans Christian Andersen's fairy tale about Ole Lukøje (Ole Shut-Eye), who squirts milk into children's eyes and has a dark brother who brings death, and pronounce the name correctly; they also mention Metallica lyrics.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the short stuff and direct listeners to HowStuffWorks.com for more.
